categories.bootstrap_multilingual: The first-run language chooser must contain multiple languages before a locale has been selected.
categories.language_data: Language-specific lexicon or matching data; changing it would alter parsing or recall behavior.
categories.prompt_fallback: Canonical Simplified-Chinese fallback behind a prompt-locale helper; locale-specific actual-send behavior is covered by prompt tests.
categories.protocol_compatibility: Stable parser token, compatibility alias, serialized marker, or example used to preserve existing data behavior.
categories.developer_diagnostic: Developer-only log, worker source, debug fixture, or internal diagnostic text that is not product UI.
categories.agent_semantic_source: Stable Maid/App Knowledge, planner, tool-observation, or retrieval semantics. This source is intentionally not mechanically translated; English output is enforced separately.
categories.canonical_localized_default: Canonical built-in content retained for identity/migration comparison and localized through a stable content or prompt ID before use.
categories.storage_internal: Persistence sentinel, legacy-data identity, migration message, or storage diagnostic; visible product chrome is covered by the UI catalog.
categories.compatibility_guidance: Compatibility-specific diagnostic text whose complete user-facing error is localized as a catalog template.

rules.reason: This chooser is rendered before locale selection and deliberately presents English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese together.
Chinese stop words and downgrade heuristics are matching data; prompt-facing labels in these modules already pass through memory prompt locale helpers.
These literals are canonical fallbacks behind prompt-locale builders; English actual-send output is asserted by prompt-locale and memory-template tests.
Remaining literals are embedded worker/runtime source, debug logs, or diagnostics; user-facing errors from these files are registered in the UI catalog.
Remaining strings are message/media sentinels, legacy Chinese parser aliases, stable role names, or embedded bridge contracts; changing them would break existing chats or imports.
The remaining bridge literals are canonical prompt fallbacks passed through prompt/memory locale helpers or stable protocol examples; all user-visible bridge chrome has moved to the UI catalog.
This Claude-compatible empty-stream suffix is part of a complete localized error template; it remains separately visible to the scanner because the runtime composes the error from two constants.

Model-facing realtime tool descriptions and task-update protocol text. The quoted confirmation keyword (允许 / yes) must match what users actually say to confirm, so it is not UI copy; user-visible strings in these files use t().

Agent-layer Han text is stable App Knowledge, intent detection, planner/tool semantics, or deterministic observations. It is not UI-copy source; English Maid responses are enforced by the prompt output-language guard and its tests.
Official default records remain canonical Chinese for migration/equality checks and are localized by stable prompt IDs only when they are still unmodified.
The bundled phone-format worldbook is a legacy protocol contract whose Chinese tags and aliases must remain parseable; it is not product chrome.
These are structured Maid memory/history labels supplied back to the planner, not UI locale strings; output language is separately constrained.

Remaining storage-layer Han text is a legacy identity/sentinel, persistence diagnostic, or migration fallback. User-visible labels and errors are handled by the UI catalog or stable content localization.
